info.name: CourtMesh API: Indian Court Cases
info.description:
# CourtMesh API: Indian court cases

A REST API over Indian court judgments and orders: the Supreme Court, every High Court, District Courts and tribunals. Search by keyword or by meaning, pull a single judgment with its parties and bench, read a structured AI analysis, follow a matter's order sheet over time, and download the source PDF.

Base URL: `https://research.courtmesh.ai/api/v1/prod`

## Getting a key

API keys are issued from the CourtMesh dashboard at https://research.courtmesh.ai. A key looks like `cm-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX-XXXX`. Keys issued before the rename start with `vv-` and still work.

## Authentication

Every endpoint except `GET /health` needs a key. Two header forms are accepted:

```
Authorization: Bearer cm-your-key-here
```

```
X-API-Key: cm-your-key-here
```

This collection uses the bearer form at the collection level, so set the `apiKey` variable once and every request inherits it.

## Collection variables

| variable | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| baseUrl | API root. Defaults to the production host |
| apiKey | Your API key. Leave it out of source control, use a Postman environment |
| caseId | A case identifier used by the case level requests. Accepts a 24 character hexadecimal case id or a case number |
| requestId | A timeline job id returned by POST /request-timeline |
| userId | A user id for GET /audit's userId query param. Call GET /me first to get your own id |
| cnr | A CNR such as DLHC010084212021, used by the CNR lookup and monitoring requests |
| watchlistId | A watchlist id (wl_...) from Create a watchlist |
| webhookId | A webhook id (wh_...) from Create a webhook |
| deliveryId | A delivery id (whd_...) from List webhook deliveries |
| changesCursor | The pagination.nextCursor from the previous List changes call |
| actSlug | An act slug such as indian-penal-code-1860, used by the Acts and Sections requests |
| sectionSlug | A provision slug such as section-302, used by the Acts and Sections requests |

## Response envelope

Every endpoint except `GET /health` returns:

```json
{ "success": true, "data": {}, "meta": {}, "pagination": {} }
```

`meta` and `pagination` appear only where the endpoint provides them. Failures return `{ "success": false, "error": "..." }`, with an extra `details` array of human readable messages when request validation failed.

Authentication and rate limit failures come from middleware and are not wrapped, they are a bare `{ "error": "..." }`.

Every response, success or failure, carries an `X-Request-Id` response header. Some endpoints (for example `GET /usage`, `POST /party/screen/batch`) also echo it as `meta.requestId` in the body; quote either one when reporting a problem to CourtMesh support.

## Rate limits

10 requests per minute per API key. Successful responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. A 429 body carries `retryAfter` in seconds and `resetTime` as an ISO timestamp. Back off and retry, do not hammer.

## Pagination

Two shapes, because the two search endpoints page differently.

`POST /search/cases` returns `{ total, hasMore, page, limit, nextCursor }`. There is no `totalPages`. For deep pagination, send the previous `nextCursor` back as `searchAfter`, in which case `page` is omitted from the response.

`POST /search/cases/semantic` returns `{ page, limit, total, totalPages, hasMore }`, where `total` and `totalPages` are estimates that only become exact on the final page.

## Idempotency

POST /party/screen, POST /party/screen/batch, POST /cases/{id}/analyze, POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated and POST /request-timeline each accept an optional `Idempotency-Key` header, 1 to 128 characters, `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`. Of the monitoring requests, only create watchlist and add cases to a watchlist honour it (the webhook requests do not take one). Every request for these endpoints in this collection carries one, defaulted to Postman's `{{$guid}}` dynamic variable (a fresh UUID v4 generated on every send).

The key is scoped per API key for 24 hours: replaying the same key with the same request body returns the original 2xx response again, with response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, and no new charge. The same key with a different body is refused with 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. A request with this key still being processed is refused with 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`. A malformed key is refused with 400 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID`.

Because `{{$guid}}` regenerates on every send, re-sending one of these requests from the Postman UI runs as a new, separately charged call each time, by design. To deliberately exercise the replay behaviour, replace the header value with a fixed string before sending the same request twice.

item.name: Search
item.description: Keyword search and semantic search over Indian court judgments.

request.description:
Keyword search across our search index of Indian court judgments.

`query` is required and must be at least one character after trimming. Everything else is optional.

Body fields:

| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| query | string | required, trimmed, minimum length 1 |
| court | string or string array | optional |
| year | integer, a four digit string, or an array of either | optional. Integers must be between 1947 and the current year |
| caseType | string or string array | optional. Values are expanded to court case type codes server side |
| caseNumber | string, or a one element string array | optional. Filters results on that single case number; a second array element is rejected with 400 ("Only one caseNumber can be filtered per request."), never silently dropped |
| judgeName | string or string array | optional |
| judges | string or string array | optional alias for judgeName |
| judge | string or string array | optional alias for judgeName |
| fromDate | string | optional, format YYYY-MM-DD |
| toDate | string | optional, format YYYY-MM-DD |
| page | integer | optional, minimum 1, default 1 |
| limit | integer | optional, 1 to 100, default 20. Each plan tier caps this lower (Free tier: 20); above the cap is rejected with 400 `PAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, and `page * limit` beyond the tier's pagination depth cap is rejected with 400 `PAGINATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` |
| cursor | string | optional opaque signed pagination cursor, the current mechanism. Send the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` back unmodified to fetch the next page; a cursor issued for a different query/filters, or a malformed one, is rejected with 400 `CURSOR_INVALID` |
| searchAfter | string | optional legacy cursor. Prefer `cursor` above for new integrations |
| sortBy | "relevance", "recent" or "oldest" | optional, default "relevance". "date" is accepted too, as a deprecated alias that is applied as "recent" |

Judge precedence in the handler is judgeName, then judges, then judge.

Response `data` is an array of raw search hits. Each hit carries the indexed document fields. Full judgment text is not stored, so `detailedSummary`, `holding`, `keyFacts_joined`, `legalIssues_joined` and `courtsReasoning` never appear here. Fetch a single case with GET /cases/{id} for the curated view.

Pagination on this endpoint is `{ total, hasMore, page, limit, nextCursor }`. There is no `totalPages`. `page` is omitted when you paginate with `cursor` or the legacy `searchAfter`.

`caseNumber` and `sortBy` are both real, honoured filters today: `caseNumber` narrows results to that single case number, and `relevance`, `recent` and `oldest` are all real sort orders (`date` silently maps to `recent`, and the response's `meta` carries a notice explaining the substitution).

{
  "query": "trade licence cancelled without notice",
  "court": "Bombay High Court",
  "year": 2021,
  "caseType": "WP",
  "judgeName": "Deshpande",
  "fromDate": "2020-01-01",
  "toDate": "2021-12-31",
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 20,
  "sortBy": "relevance"
}

query.description: Set to true to start a live court fetch when the CNR is not in the corpus.

request.description:
Look a case up by its CNR (Case Number Record). Any common spelling is accepted and normalised: the path value is trimmed, uppercased, and spaces, hyphens, slashes, dots and a leading `CNR`, `CNR:` or `CNR NO` are removed. A valid CNR is 16 characters, for example `DLHC010084212021`; anything else is 400 `INVALID_CNR`.

Costs 1 credit, charged only when a record is returned (`not_found` and `pending` cost 0).

`data.status` is `found` (200, `data.case` is the same record `GET /cases/{id}` returns, including `caseStatus`, `caseStage`, `nextHearingDate`, `lastListedOn` and `orderCount`), `pending` (202, a live fetch is running: poll this same URL; `requestId` is opaque and is not accepted by `GET /get-timeline`), or `not_found` (404 with code `CASE_NOT_FOUND`; the error body also carries `cnr` and `status`). A Supreme Court CNR that is not in the corpus cannot be fetched live and is `404` at once.

Set `fetch=true` to start a live court fetch for a CNR that is not in the corpus: the call that starts the fetch returns `202 pending` and is free; the poll that returns the record is the one 1 credit charge, and a fetch the court portal cannot satisfy is free. Fetches share the daily live fetch cap with `POST /request-timeline` `refresh: true`.

If the court portal had nothing for the CNR in the last 24 hours, `fetch=true` does not ask it again: the call answers `404 CASE_NOT_FOUND` straight away. A case taken down at a party's request is reported as not found.

item.name: Monitoring
item.description: Watch CNRs and be told when something changes. Create a watchlist, read the change feed with `GET /changes`, and optionally receive the same events as signed webhooks. Watchlist and webhook management, the daily check of every watched CNR, and webhook delivery are free; only reading the change feed costs credits (1 per non-empty page of up to 100 events). New error codes: `INVALID_CNR`, `WATCHLIST_NOT_FOUND`, `WEBHOOK_NOT_FOUND`, `DELIVERY_NOT_FOUND`, `WATCH_CAP_EXCEEDED`, `WATCHLIST_LIMIT_REACHED`, `WEBHOOK_LIMIT_REACHED`, `INVALID_WEBHOOK_URL`, `ITEM_NOT_FOUND`. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` on the Indian calendar; a court's year 9999 "no date" is returned as null. A case taken down at a party's request shows as an `unavailable` item, sends no events, and cannot be added (the add returns `not_found`). API keys with explicit scopes need `monitoring:read` and `monitoring:write`.

header.description: Optional, 1 to 128 characters, [A-Za-z0-9_.-]. Scoped per API key for 24 hours: a replayed request with the same key and the same body returns the stored 2xx response again (response header Idempotency-Replayed: true, no new charge). Postman's {{$guid}} generates a fresh UUID v4 per send; paste a fixed value to test the replay behaviour deliberately.

request.description:
Create a named set of CNRs to monitor. Body: `{ name (1..100 chars), items? (up to 100), metadata? (up to 2 KB) }`. Each item is `{ cnr, reference? (your own id, up to 200 chars, echoed on every event), label? (up to 200 chars) }`.

Free: watchlist management costs 0 credits, and the daily monitoring check of every watched CNR is included. Watched CNR caps per account: Free 10, Pay As You Go 1,000, Scale 10,000, Enterprise by contract; at most 50 watchlists. The cap counts distinct CNRs across all watchlists, so the same CNR on two lists uses one slot. Two daily limits apply to adding, counted per Indian calendar day: every add that results in a watched or pending item counts toward a daily add allowance per account (Free 50, Pay As You Go 5,000, Scale 50,000, Enterprise 500,000), and adding CNRs that are not in the corpus yet starts a live fetch, so those also have their own daily limit (Free 20, Pay As You Go 500, Scale 5,000, Enterprise unlimited). Items over either come back `cap_exceeded` with a message. `not_found`, `error` and `unavailable` items still count toward the cap until removed.

The response is the watchlist plus one result per item: `watching`, `pending` (not in the corpus, so a live fetch was started), `invalid`, `duplicate`, `cap_exceeded` or `not_found`. A Supreme Court CNR that is not in the corpus is `not_found` at once, and so is a CNR the court portal had nothing for in the last 24 hours (no new fetch is started until that cooldown passes) or a case that was taken down. A CNR already in the corpus is `watching` at once; its `case.tracking_started` event is sent when the first fresh refresh completes, or immediately if the stored record is already current. A partial success is still HTTP 200. The call is refused with 403 `WATCH_CAP_EXCEEDED` only when the cap is already full and at least one new CNR was sent. `Idempotency-Key` is honoured on this request.

The change feed across all your watchlists, oldest first, in the order the events were recorded. 1 credit per page of up to 100 events; an empty page costs 0. `pagination.nextCursor` is opaque (store it and send it back, never build or parse it) and is always returned, even on an empty page, so a client can poll forward indefinitely. `since` is converted to a feed position once; the cursor you get back continues from there.

An event appears in the feed about 2 seconds after it is created. `types` values outside the known list match nothing.

`case.tracking_started` is sent once the first fresh refresh of a case completes (immediately if the stored record is already current), not at the moment of the add. A burst of new orders announces only the newest 20, oldest first, and an order dated more than 7 days before you started watching is never announced to you. A case taken down at a party's request sends no events.

request.description:
Register an HTTPS endpoint. Body: `{ url, events? (default all case.* types), watchlistIds? (default all), description? (up to 200 chars) }`. Without `events` the response and later reads echo the full default `case.*` list; without `watchlistIds` they echo `[]`, which means all watchlists. `Idempotency-Key` is honoured on this request. At most 10 endpoints per account. Returns HTTP 201. Free.

The response includes `secret` (`whsec_` plus 32 random bytes, base64url), shown only here and on rotate. Store it: use it with the SDK helper `verifyWebhookSignature` / `verify_webhook_signature`.

URL rules: https only, port 443 or any non privileged port, and the hostname must resolve to a public address at create time and again at every delivery.

Each delivery is a POST with the event as JSON and headers `CourtMesh-Event-Id`, `CourtMesh-Event-Type`, `CourtMesh-Delivery-Id` and `CourtMesh-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")>` (two `v1=` values during a secret rotation). Success is any 2xx within 10 seconds (each attempt reads at most 64 KB of your response); redirects are not followed. Retries after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h and 24 h, then `failed`. A delivery that could not be attempted within 24 hours is marked `failed` with `lastError: "expired"` instead of being sent.

request.description:
List every stored document that shares this case's case number, plus a derived hearing timeline.

request.description:
Get an encrypted, time limited download link for the case PDF.

The `id` path parameter accepts either a 24 character hexadecimal case id or a case number. The case id is tried first, then the case number.

`data.pdfUrl` is ciphertext, not a URL you can fetch directly. It is a time limited link that expires after `data.expiresIn` seconds, which is 3600. It is decrypted by the CourtMesh SDKs.

Code `PDF_NOT_STORED` means the case exists but has no stored document, and carries a `hint` field pointing at POST /request-timeline with `refresh: true`, which can fetch orders for High Court and District Court cases (tribunal documents are not fetchable via this API).

request.description:

request.description:
Queue AI analysis for one case. The call returns immediately with 202 and the work continues in the background.

The `id` path parameter accepts either a 24 character hexadecimal case id or a case number. The case id is tried first, then the case number.

Body: `{ "force": false, "allowRemoteFetch": false }`. Both fields are optional and default to false.

`force`: send `true` to re-run analysis on a case that already has one (also billed again).

`allowRemoteFetch`: required before the server will fetch this case's source document from a remote court host, when it is not already available as stored text or a stored document (only approved court and official sources are ever eligible). Without it, a case that needs a remote fetch to be analyzed returns 403 `REMOTE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED` instead of running. When a remote fetch actually happens, a 20 credit surcharge is added on top of the base analyze price. Not available on the Free tier, which returns 403 `REMOTE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED` regardless of this flag.

Responses:
- 202 when the job was queued. `data` is `{ message: "Analysis has been started", status: "processing" }`. Poll GET /cases/{id} and watch `hasAnalysis`, or read GET /cases/{id}/analysis, after 30 to 60 seconds.
- 200 when an analysis already exists and `force` was not set. `data` is `{ message: "Analysis already exists", analysis: { ... }, alreadyExists: true }`.
- 400 when the case has neither at least 100 characters of stored text nor an attached document.
- 403 `API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED` on the Free tier, which has no AI analysis allowance at all.
- 403 `REMOTE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED` when the document needs a remote fetch and `allowRemoteFetch` was not sent, or the tier does not allow it, or the host is outside the allowed list.

The analysis runs against the stored judgment PDF when one is available, and falls back to the extracted text otherwise.

**Credits.** This call costs 100 credits per run, plus a further 20 credit surcharge when the source document actually had to be fetched remotely, charged when the job is queued; a cached `alreadyExists` response is not charged again. Not available on the free tier: this endpoint, POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated and GET /cases/{id}/analysis all return 403 with code `API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED` and an upgrade URL on the free tier, which has no AI analysis allowance at all.

item.description: Party name screening against the case corpus for KYC, background verification, due diligence, counterparty and compliance workflows. The same key with a different body is refused with 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a request with this key already in flight is refused with 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS; a malformed key is refused with 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID. request.description:
Screen one person or company name against the case corpus for litigation history: KYC, background verification (BGV), due diligence, counterparty and compliance checks.

Body fields:

| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | string | required, 2 to 200 characters |
| aliases | string array | optional, at most 7 - name plus aliases must fit the 8 name screening limit |
| entityType | "person" or "company" | required |
| purpose | "kyc", "bgv", "due_diligence", "litigation", "research" or "compliance" | required, see the DPDP note below |
| identifiers | object `{ pan, gstin, cin, llpin }` | optional, all sub fields optional strings, each format checked |
| address | object `{ city, state, stateCode }` | optional |
| knownPersons | string array | optional, at most 10, directors/partners/associates used to disambiguate |
| court | string, or a one element string array | optional, restrict to one court - a second court in the array is rejected with 400 ("one court per request for now") |
| since | string | optional, YYYY-MM-DD. Best effort post filter; using it at all forces `verdict` to `inconclusive`, see below |
| limit | integer | optional, 1 to 100, default 40 |
| adjudicate | boolean | optional, default false, see credits and the Free tier note below |
| displayThreshold | number | optional, 0 to 1, default 0.6, confidence cutoff for inclusion in `matches` |

**purpose is required under DPDP.** It is recorded as the lawful basis for processing this name and is not decorative: pick the value that genuinely describes why the screen is being run.

**A match is a case record bearing the name, not a verified identity.** Common names, aliases and identical company names across unrelated parties all produce matches. Read `confidence.band`, `evidence.matchedFields` and `evidence.disambiguatorPresent` on every match before treating it as identity confirmed, and prefer matches corroborated by an identifier (PAN, GSTIN, CIN, LLPIN) or address over name only matches. `confidence` is `{ band, score, calibrated, engine }`: `band` is one of `confirmed`, `probable`, `possible` or `unlikely`; `score` and `calibrated` are the same number (`score` is kept as a stable top level alias); `engine` is `"rules"` or `"llm"` depending on whether adjudication actually ran for that candidate. `evidence.signals` is an array of `{ name, status, weight, evidence }` objects, one per matching signal considered (for example a GSTIN match or a name similarity score), not plain strings.

**Verdict semantics.** `data.summary.verdict` is one of `matches_found`, `no_matches_found` or `inconclusive`, and the rules are stricter than they look:
- `no_matches_found` is only ever returned when `data.coverage.exhaustive` is true (every available search strategy actually ran to completion) AND nothing was withheld.

item.description: Public corpus coverage and freshness snapshot. No API key required.

request.description:
Corpus coverage and freshness snapshot: total records, a breakdown by court type and by year, per court figures, and a rolled up District Court row (the index has no state field for district courts yet).

No API key required. Cached server side, see `meta.cacheTtlSeconds`; treat `data.generatedAt` as the figure's as-of time rather than expecting a live count on every call.

Each row (`byCourtType`, `courts`, `districtCourts`) uses `records` for its count, not `total`. `documentBearing` (a count of records that also have the order or judgment text indexed) and, at the top level only, `statusOnly` are OPTIONAL and OMITTED BY DEFAULT at every level they could appear (top level, each `byCourtType` row, each `courts` row, `districtCourts`) - the document-bearing versus status-only split is behind a publish flag (`COVERAGE_PUBLISH_DOCUMENT_SHARE`, default off) and is not disclosed until a human turns it on, so do not assume it is present.

request.description:
Deep health check. The plain GET /health above is a cheap liveness probe, no dependency calls, always fast, always 200 while the process is up. Adding ?deep=1 also checks core dependencies (each bounded to a short timeout) and returns a checks object, one entry per dependency: { status: "ok" | "degraded" | "down", latencyMs, error? }.

status on this form is "healthy", "degraded" or "unhealthy"; HTTP 503 (status: "unhealthy") means a hard dependency is down. No API key required, not rate limited beyond the public health limiter.
